The workstation's source builds run as two units from values-free templates. adoption/templates/systemd/omniroute.service runs 20128, the shared gateway: build cf6748d04, with the local affinity patch and upstream PR #15167, so no OAuth routing combo may be created on 20128 while the affinity patch runs. adoption/templates/systemd/omniroute-fw.service runs 20129, the framework instance: build 87c4c488d, with its own data directory, forwarding to 20128 through a provider node. Both units announce CODEX_CLIENT_VERSION 0.159.1 while the installed Codex is 0.157.1, so the gateway's live catalog lists gpt-6.1-sol. 20129 runs ten of the twelve shipped compression engines at upstream's per-engine settings with the master switch on (upstream ships the master off and every engine disabled; headroom is off in the engines map but still runs where a stored combo names it, omniglyph is off; headerless plan session-dedup, ccr, lite; lossy engines only on a header or combo opt-in; the header allow-lossy selects a peer-owned stored combo); 20128 keeps its master switch off with codex/* excluded. Serve's port preflight counts client sockets on the port; 20128's prefix carries lsof shim v2, which leaves the bind probe as the guard, so a client's dead connection no longer blocks its restart, while 20129 and the previous 20128 prefix still have v1 (restart hindsight-live and any other client holding a connection first). The gateway is adopted for pooled GPT-6 access by gateway-routed Codex lanes. By the user's decision 20128 runs keyless and passwordless on loopback only (docs/decisions/2026-09-27-omniroute-account-pool.md, decision 5); 20129 also binds loopback only. A multi-user or non-loopback host keeps this recipe's API key and dashboard login. Native Codex stays the max-quality default, and the agent-sdks layer default waits on the preregistered three-arm comparison. Existing native accounts, models, hooks and default routing remain unchanged. Local preview success does not establish semantic fidelity or provider-token savings.
